Verified upstream v-model/controlled-uncontrolled contract: modelValue/defaultValue props, d_value internal state, controlled computed detecting whether modelValue was actually passed. Ultimate decision: excludes the live, working @primevue/forms integration ($pcForm/$pcFormField injection, formField.onChange, $formNovalidate/$formValue/$formDefaultValue/$formControl) entirely — a deliberate boundary cut of a real feature, per spec §19/§20's resolved fork (Gate 6 #2), not an absence-of-feature finding. Implementation-time deviation from the task brief's draft: verified BaseEditableHolder.vue's controlled computed uses this.$inProps.hasOwnProperty('modelValue'), where $inProps (Vue-internal, seen in BaseComponent.vue) is itself built from Object.keys(this.$.vnode?.props || {}) filtered against declared prop keys. The brief's draft controlled implementation approximated this via an $attrs/prop-value-presence check; testing (base-editable-holder.spec.ts's __draft-check scratch verification, not committed) proved this draft diverges from real $inProps semantics in a concrete case: modelValue passed explicitly as undefined while defaultValue is also passed with a real value — real PrimeVue says controlled=true (modelValue key present wins), the draft said controlled=false (wrong). Final implementation reads this.$.vnode.props directly (the same public component-instance surface $inProps itself uses, accessible via Options-API `this.$`), checking key presence for both modelValue/model-value and defaultValue/default-value to be resilient to Vue's prop-name normalization. Verified correct against all 4 brief test cases plus the divergence edge case.
Ultimate-authored test, not derived from upstream.

Consumes @ultimate/uix-utils/escape's shared priority-tuple registry (extracted from react-core/src/escape/use-global-escape-key.ts during Phase 4's prerequisite work, Task 1); PrimeVue's own Dialog.vue keydown listener has no equivalent stacking mechanism (verified gap, spec §11). This file supplies only the Vue mixin mounted/updated/beforeUnmount lifecycle wiring — not a react-core dependency. Implementation-time deviation from the task brief's draft: the draft's unregister() re-read the priority getter to determine which secondary value to unregister, which is wrong when the getter's underlying value already changed before updated() fires (Vue evaluates the getter fresh both times within the same synchronous updated() call) — this leaves the OLD tuple registered forever as a stale leak while also registering the NEW one, so both point at the same callback. Final implementation instead tracks the actually-registered secondary value in a closure variable and unregisters exactly that value, unconditionally of what the getter currently returns. Caught by escape.spec.ts's dedicated re-registration test (secondary moving from a high value to a low one, with a competitor in between) — RED against the draft's literal logic, GREEN against the fix.

Verified upstream sentinel-span + MutationObserver mechanism (spec §14): two hidden focusable spans bracketing trapped content, each redirecting focus to the first/last real focusable descendant on focus; a MutationObserver redirects focus if lost after a dynamic-content change. disabled=true/false explicit two-state contract matches verified source exactly. Reuses existing @ultimate/uix-utils/dom's getFirstFocusableElement/getLastFocusableElement/focus/createElement (already-built Phase 1 primitives, confirmed present verbatim). Does not restore focus on unmount (verified absent upstream) — UDialog's own responsibility. Implementation-time verification: the sentinel redirect logic (onFirstHiddenFocus/onLastHiddenFocus) depends on the focus event's relatedTarget correctly reflecting the previously-focused element for the wraparound branch to fire — confirmed directly against jsdom (a scratch test, not committed) that native .focus() calls populate relatedTarget from the prior activeElement exactly like a real browser Tab traversal, while a bare `dispatchEvent(new FocusEvent('focus'))` does not carry a relatedTarget and does not exercise the wraparound branch. The MutationObserver's dynamic-content redirect was verified directly by removing a focused element from a mounted component and confirming document.activeElement moved to the next real focusable after a microtask flush — jsdom's MutationObserver behaves synchronously enough for this to be reliably testable.

Verified upstream: BaseFocusTrap.extend('focustrap', { style: FocusTrapStyle }) — this file's Ultimate equivalent uses the createDirective factory (Task 6) instead; no separate BaseFocusTrap-equivalent file needed since createDirective already supplies the shared factory shape.

Ultimate-authored test, not derived from upstream (PrimeVue's own FocusTrap.js has no dedicated spec file). Extends the brief's draft 4-test list with 2 additional tests: a real MutationObserver dynamic-content-redirect test (removing a focused element and verifying document.activeElement moves to the next real focusable after a microtask flush) and a disabled-transitions-to-true unbind test (verifying the observer no longer reacts to DOM mutations after `updated` calls `unbind`). The brief's draft 4th test (Shift+Tab wraparound) used a bare `dispatchEvent(new FocusEvent('focus'))` with no relatedTarget, which does not exercise the real wraparound branch (verified — relatedTarget is null on a bare dispatch, routing to the non-wraparound branch instead); rewritten to focus the first real element then call `.focus()` natively on the first sentinel, letting jsdom populate relatedTarget the way a real browser Tab does.
